title: Conjecture 5
statement_text: For an $n$-set with a random partition with probabilities $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$, the clique algorithm has minimal average complexity among all AC algorithms.
context_text: An active clustering (AC) algorithm must recover an unknown partition of an $n$-set by queries asking an oracle whether two given items belong to the same class; it uses transitivity (never querying a pair whose relation is already implied) and stops once every class is known to be connected by positive answers and every pair of classes has received at least one negative answer. Its average complexity is the expected number of queries for a random input partition. In the model considered, each item independently belongs to class $C_i$ with probability $p_i$, for a fixed number $k$ of classes with $p_1\ge\dots\ge p_k$, $\sum_ip_i=1$. The clique algorithm processes items one by one and compares each new item with one representative of each block discovered so far, in decreasing order of block size, until it is added to a block or a new block is created. For uniformly random partitions the authors prove that an AC algorithm has minimal average complexity iff it is chordal (the graph of known negative answers between aggregated blocks stays chordal), and that all chordal algorithms, including the clique algorithm, have the same query distribution. For the $p_i$-model they prove that the clique algorithm makes $\mathbb{E}[X]\sim n\sum_{i=1}^kip_i$ queries, fewer than the algorithm choosing random unresolved pairs. The conjecture is that no AC algorithm does better on average in the $p_i$-model.
paper_title: Active clustering for labeling training data
